stories.title: It Sprouts Only Here
stories.excerpt: Rain falls beyond the circle; the seed tells its secret only to the ground beneath it.
stories.body: 小当归 found a seed on the paper ground. Instead of putting it in an envelope or asking the wind to carry it away, 小当归 rolled over each day to shield it from hurried rain. On the third morning, two leaves appeared, their roots staying quietly below. 小当归 watched for a long time and understood: not everything grows by traveling farther. Some things grow because they are carefully allowed to remain where they belong.
stories.alt: A circle of warm light shelters 小当归 and a new sprout beneath a pale blue rain wash.
stories.productTheme: Local-only records; data stays on the device

stories.title: Planting Today
stories.excerpt: Today was too large for a pocket, so 小当归 folded it into paper seeds.
stories.body: Today was rather long: buy a light bulb, answer a letter, and remember to water the plant at dusk. 小当归 tried to push the whole day into a pocket and rolled out first. So the day became several small slips, folded and planted one by one in warm paper soil. The Tasks did not become fewer, but they suddenly had an order. When the last slip was gently marked done, a tiny green shoot appeared from the ground.
stories.alt: 小当归 keeps watch beside a folded paper seed and a new sprout, with wide warm-paper space to the left.

stories.title: Past Has Rings of Its Own
stories.excerpt: A finished thing did not vanish; it followed the paper river into a new ring.
stories.body: 小当归 placed a completed Task in the paper river, expecting it to drift away like a leaf. The next day, the paper had curled into a pale tree ring, with room beside it for another line. More finished things joined it, and the river slowly lengthened. 小当归 sometimes returned to change a sentence or add a detail. Past, it turned out, was not a sealed box. It was one long document that could still breathe and grow.
stories.alt: 小当归 stands by a paper river as a leaf settles into softly glowing concentric rings.
stories.productTheme: Past; completed Tasks in an editable long-form document

stories.title: One Very Gentle Reminder
stories.excerpt: The bell flower made only one ripple—just enough to bring the note back to mind.
stories.body: The bell flower promised to remind 小当归 when the moon rose. It did not shout or chase anyone around the garden. At the agreed time, it released one thin circle through the air. 小当归 tilted slightly, noticed the note by its side, and remembered to water the plant near the window. Once the Task was done, the bell flower lowered its head again. The Reminder had finished its work, and the garden returned to being quiet.
stories.alt: Under moonlight, a bell flower sends out a soft ripple while 小当归 listens beside a folded note.

stories.title: Even Blank Things Can Be Kept
stories.excerpt: A note without a title may simply be waiting for a sentence that has not arrived yet.
stories.body: 小当归 found a blank sheet with no title on the front and no full stop on the back. The wind said it was useless and should be allowed to fly away. 小当归 carried it home with two very short arms and placed it among the Notes. Days later, a sentence appeared during a walk and landed neatly on that waiting page. Blankness was not a mistake after all. It had simply saved a place for something that was not ready yet.
stories.alt: In a warm watercolor garden, 小当归 gently stores a blank sheet in a paper box beside the plants.
stories.productTheme: Notes; untitled Notes can be saved and continued

stories.title: The Paper Plane That Was Not Sent
stories.excerpt: The plane did not travel far; it rested comfortably on the same sheet of paper.
stories.body: 小当归 folded a paper plane and tucked a thought meant only for itself into the crease. The wind knocked and asked whether the plane should be carried far away. After thinking, 小当归 tied on a thin thread, let the plane make one small circle indoors, and watched it land nearby. The secret was neither taken nor made lighter. It simply stayed in place, ready to be opened again whenever 小当归 chose.
stories.alt: 小当归 holds a thread attached to a blank paper plane resting nearby, with a two-leaf plant behind it.
stories.productTheme: Privacy; no uploads and no account

stories.title: A Bookmark for Yesterday
stories.excerpt: Yesterday was finished, but not locked; 小当归 could still add one true sentence.
stories.body: 小当归 opened yesterday and noticed the smell after the rain had been forgotten. Yesterday felt awkward and said it had already passed. Still, 小当归 slipped a small bookmark from the edge of the paper roll and added: “like freshly washed bark.” Yesterday did not crack, and today did not become untidy. The record simply became a little more true. Finished Tasks, Past, and Notes could still be revisited, edited, and cared for.
stories.alt: 小当归 watches blank slips become a long rolled paper path stretching toward a distant sprout.
stories.productTheme: Reliable editing; Tasks, Past, and Notes remain editable

stories.title: Rain Sounds in a Small Wooden Box
stories.excerpt: 小当归 made a backup of the rain; whether the box had a lock was its own choice.
stories.body: The rain sounded especially good, and 小当归 worried that tomorrow might forget it. The sound was folded into a small paper slip and placed in a wooden box. 小当归 opened the box once more to make sure no corner of the rain was missing, then closed the lid. A lock could be added, but then its key had to be remembered. The box would not run away; it would wait locally until the rain needed to be restored.
stories.alt: In a rainy watercolor garden, 小当归 collects drops and ripples in a wooden box beside an open lock and key.
stories.productTheme: Local backup; optional encryption and validation before restore
